  WHY: An operator implementing the rename instruction literally for merged sessions would omit the required issue prefix, leading to inconsistent session sidebar visibility and violating the project-wide requirement that all numbered session titles must lead with their issue number.

  Evidence of absence: The set_session_title rename instruction is explicitly implemented only in steps 3a (line 25) and 6 (line 38); steps 8 (line 53), 10 (line 67), 11 (line 73), and 12 (line 77) lack this instruction, leaving these automation stages unnumbered.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR

  Evidence of absence: The test implementation asserts rename instructions only for steps 3a and 6, failing to verify that the renaming requirement is met for steps 8, 10, 11, and 12.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  Expected change site: tests/test_session_titles.py, the test_checker_titles_old_new_and_hand_prefixed_all_match parametrised block.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: tests/test_session_titles.py
  Line or code reference: test_stage_renames_itself_when_it_opens_a_pr (around lines 70-75)
  Requirement: "A stage that opens a PR (steps 3a, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12) renames itself with `set_session_title` in that same step" (Session titles rule, workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md around line 135) — the rule names six PR-opening steps.
  Expected change site: tests/test_session_titles.py::test_stage_renames_itself_when_it_opens_a_pr
  Evidence of absence: The test asserts `Record \`Final PR: #F\` in the log ... rename this session with that PR per [Session titles](#session-titles).` and `Record the PR number in the log (\`Waiting on: PR #N\`), and rename this session with the phase PR per [Session titles](#session-titles).` (steps 3a and 6 only). It does not assert that steps 8 (conformance fix), 10 (validation fix), 11 (completion PR), or 12 (verify-activation fix) carry any equivalent rename cross-reference, leaving four of the six rule-named steps untested. The project log marks this as "Rejected (by design)" with the rationale that the Session titles rule itself is the instruction and a stage reads the whole file — but the rule's literal text is the only thing pinning this behavior, so a future edit that drops the cross-reference on one of those steps without a test will not be caught.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md and .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: Session titles rule (line ~135) names steps 3a, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12; rename cross-references appear only in steps 3a (~line 25) and 6 (~line 38)
  Requirement: "A stage that opens a PR (steps 3a, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12) renames itself with `set_session_title` in that same step" — the rule names all six steps.
  Expected change site: steps 8 (conformance fix), 10 (validation fix), 11 (completion PR), and 12 (verify-activation fix) of the command file
  Evidence of absence: grep for `rename this session` in the twin file finds matches only at line 25 (step 3a) and line 38 (step 6). Steps 8, 10, 11, and 12 open PRs on `claude/implement-plan-<slug>-{conformance,validation,activation}-fix-…` and `-complete` branches but contain no `set_session_title` cross-reference. The rule explicitly says the rename happens "in that same step", so a stage session running one of those steps and following the rule literally would still need to discover the rename instruction by reading the Session titles subsection — workable, but fragile. This matches the same gap flagged in earlier review rounds (consensus task gap with confidence 5) and the project log's "Rejected (by design)" verdict with AD-1.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
